##  · K3-irq-level-latch — Follow-up (K3 owner): an IRQ raised while its object is masked, before a driver's first receive, can be lost

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `ec5214a2d73ce31fdc5a1652662215f0` · 2026-09-24T23:11:31Z

> From K5 review 5. The goldfish RTC alarm on QEMU virt: an interrupt raised while its IRQ object is masked (between receives) was not delivered to the next receive, but only on the driver's first receive (trial 0); later masked raises and fresh edges were delivered 5/5 and 6/6. A reading found no kernel defect. Action: add an irq-level-latch boot case (raise with the object masked before the first receive, then expect delivery) and fix whatever it finds (kernel IRQ object initial state, PLIC claim or enable ordering, or a QEMU quirk). Mitigation meanwhile: netd drains its used rings after DRIVER_OK and after every receive (asked of D3). Schedule it with K6 or a small K3 follow-up.
